specification.problem: Reconstruct a minimal mathematical framework for universal quantum computation with interacting bosonic quantum walkers on a graph under the Bose-Hubbard model, with qubits encoded in walker positions. The paper-specific graph geometry, gate constructions and parameters are not given in the abstract.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful instance (an assumption): one walker on a two-vertex graph encoding one qubit, with a tunneling-generated X rotation and an on-site-energy-generated Z rotation, plus the generic Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian as background. Outside this scope: the actual piecewise-constant graph design, the cphase and swap constructions, linear-vertex scaling, Steane code encoding, 3D extension, and the optical lattice implementation.

symbols.meaning: bosonic creation and annihilation operators at vertex i
hopping amplitude between adjacent vertices i and j
logical qubit states, assumed to be the walker at vertex 1 or vertex 2

equations.label: Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian
equations.latex: H=-\sum_{\langle i,j\rangle}J_{ij}\left(a_i^\dagger a_j+a_j^\dagger a_i\right)+\sum_i \epsilon_i n_i+\frac{U}{2}\sum_i n_i(n_i-1)
equations.description: Generic Bose-Hubbard model on a graph, which the abstract says is two-dimensional.
equations.justification: The abstract names the Bose-Hubbard model but gives no explicit Hamiltonian, so this is the textbook form. The paper's parameters and graph are unknown.

equations.label: Position encoding of one qubit
equations.description: One walker on two vertices encodes one qubit.
equations.justification: The abstract says information is encoded in walker positions. The two-vertex dual-rail form is an assumed minimal instance.
assumptions: The paper's actual encoding may differ

equations.label: X rotation by tunneling
equations.latex: H_X=-J\left(a_1^\dagger a_2+a_2^\dagger a_1\right),\quad U_X(\theta)=e^{-iH_Xt}=e^{i J t X_L},\ \theta=-2Jt
equations.description: Within the single-walker subspace, hopping acts as a logical X rotation, with the convention R_X(\theta)=e^{-i\theta X/2}.
equations.justification: Direct consequence of eq_1 restricted to one particle on two sites. It is not the paper's specific scheme.
assumptions: Single walker so U is irrelevant

equations.label: Z rotation by potential offset
equations.description: With hopping off, a relative on-site energy gives a logical Z rotation.
equations.justification: The relative phase between the two position states follows from eq_1 with J=0. The paper's mechanism for Z rotations is unknown.
assumptions: Hopping can be switched or localized

equations.label: Target gate set
equations.description: Target two-qubit gate definitions, with the cphase phase \varphi left unspecified.
equations.abstract_quote: an entangling two-qubit cphase gate and a swap gate
equations.justification: The abstract names the gates. Their matrices are standard definitions, but the bosonic construction is not given.

registers.name: walker position register
registers.size: 2 vertices per qubit in the assumed minimal instance; unknown in the paper's scheme (linear in the number of qubits)
registers.role: Encodes the logical qubit by the walker's location

specification.initial_state: Assumed: one walker at vertex 1, |0>_L = a_1^\dagger|vac>.

steps.description: Prepare the walker at a chosen vertex to initialize the logical state.
Apply an X rotation by evolving under hopping for time t.
Apply a Z rotation by evolving under a relative on-site potential with hopping off.
Entangling cphase and swap gates are required for universality, but the interacting multi-walker construction is not specified in the abstract.

specification.measurement: Single-qubit measurement by localized position (occupation) measurement, as the abstract suggests localized operators. The details are not given.
assumptions: The smallest instance is chosen by the reconstructor, since no scope was given.
The single-walker two-vertex model is only illustrative; the paper's piecewise-constant graph and parameters are unknown.
